brief: Equities are reverting higher on Nov 6 (NDX > RTY > SPX) after a whipsaw week, with SPX ticking just above its 200dma even though over 60% of constituents are red. A strong NFP print (165k vs 70k expected) accompanies the bounce; VIX is normalizing to a 25-handle after its largest one-day change since Covid, and WTI is down slightly under $90. The move follows yesterday's historic selloff: NDX (+1.3%) is rebounding from its worst day since March 2020, Goldman's High Beta Momentum basket (+2.4%) from a 6.2% drop that left it down 51% from June highs, and the SOX (+3%) from its worst day since 2020. TMT flow lacks conviction and stays muted, with balanced flows and modest dip-buying. Hedge fund performance was hit hard yesterday: Global Fundamental L/S managers fell 1.3% (-2SD) on beta exposure, and GS Prime saw more hedging via Macro Products, though not panic-driven degrossing; 7 of 11 sectors were net sold. Liquidity stayed thin ($4mm average, now $3mm), ETF volumes stayed elevated (35% of tape), and CTAs are projected to keep selling SPX/NDX next week. Goldman's own flows skew to the buy side across LOs and HFs.
